newsitem.title: USA: Copper smelter bottleneck to ease - ASARCO.
newsitem.headline: Copper smelter bottleneck to ease - ASARCO.

text.p: The bottleneck in copper smelting capacity remains tight, but an easing is on the horizon and spot treatment and refining charges have already edged off their recent highs, ASARCO's chairman, Richard De J Osborne told analysts.
"I think the smelter market is at its tightest right now," Osborne said.

Treatment and refining charges (TFRC) - the amount of money a miner pays a smelter to process copper concentrates into metal - have soared to a peak of 40 cents per pound, but backed off a couple of cents in the past few weeks, he added.
In 1994 TCRCs were about 13.5 cents per pound.
High TCRCs forced ASARCO to partially curtail operatations at one of its two concentrators at its Ray Complex in the U.S. earlier this year.
ASARCO was producing more concs that it consumed at its own smelter. It was not economic to sell the surplus.
"There is virtually no market in the West for copper concentrates," Osborne said.
"The only country that has taken concentrates is China...but you have huge transporation costs to get it there," he added.
More "normal" levels of TCRCs would be 20 to 25 cents per pound.

A number of smelter expansions are underway, along with new smelters under construction in China. "If these come on stream as projected, that should alleviate some of the real tightness that we are seeing," Osborne said.
He expected about one million tons of new smelter capacity on stream by the end of 1997, but saw no further new smelters being built in the U.S. because of tough environmental requirements.
